about: Curated input of the UI hazard scan (python -m civ5headless.hazards). methods: DLL Lua methods known to change game state although the source derivation misses them or names them less clearly. engine: Lua calls that the real game turns into DLL calls and the host does not. notHazards: derived methods that do not change state after all (vetted). harmlessCaches: functions that write a cache whose value does not depend on when it is computed (lookup indexes, scratch buffers); the derivation does not follow them. writesWithArgs: methods that change state only when called with at least minArgs arguments; calls with fewer are not hazards. notWithDll (on a method): with a run report whose dll section has these values, the method does not change state (the hit is covered, reason notWithDllWhy). reviews: hits reviewed by hand, matched by file name and optionally methods, a function regular expression, lines or sha256; verdict input (reached only through player input although the scan cannot tell) or covered (the host does the same, or the call is harmless), with why.

methods.name: Rand
methods.why: advances the game's synchronised random number generator (CvGame::getJonRandNum): every later random draw changes

methods.name: Rand
methods.why: advances the map random number generator (CvGame::getMapRandNum)

methods.name: CalculateGoldRate
methods.why: stock BNW and VP before the 2026 determinism fix: the treasury cost calculation stores the unit maintenance (CvTreasury::m_iExpensePerTurnUnitMaintenance, saved)
methods.notWithDllWhy: the run's DLL is this fork's (it reports digest additions), which has the determinism fix: CalculateGoldRate no longer stores the unit maintenance (CvTreasury::GetExpensePerTurnUnitMaintenance computes it); M5 parity runs identical

methods.name: GetMilitaryMight
methods.why: lazy: recomputed at most once per turn (stock: elapsed turn, VP: turn slice) and stored; which caller comes first decides the stored value

methods.name: GetPower
methods.why: calls the military might getter (lazy, as GetMilitaryMight)

the Squads add-in runs in the host: SquadsOptions.lua (included) fires SQUADS_OPTIONS_CHANGED at load as in the game, and from its option buttons (input). The options come from the user's mod data, which the host keeps empty: with a saved end-movement option the real game sets it on the active player's units at load. M5 parity runs identical
